retrieval_gate.rationale: The defect is causally located at an existing budget-policy boundary: ContextCompressor computes its trigger from the raw context window even though the transport reserves max_tokens from that same window. The intended threshold is therefore derived from the observable effective input capacity, context_length minus the resolved output cap, rather than by changing downstream compaction behavior. The visible focused tests lock the corrected value, unchanged no-reservation behavior, degenerate-window fallback, and invalid-value coercion, matching the pattern's repair-at-policy-boundary and neighboring-regression requirements. The repository-specific workflow candidates concern different mechanisms, such as shell-output truncation or model-alias classification, so the cross-workflow budget-policy pattern is the applicable candidate.

weight_basis.policy: Correctness receives the majority weight because repository-level coding benchmarks treat issue resolution through regression tests as the primary outcome. Quality and efficiency are reported separately and only break ties between oracle-passing arms. The 60/25/15 split is an AREX operational choice, not a weight copied from any cited benchmark.

judge.rationale: The patch makes the compaction threshold reservation-aware by computing it from the effective input window, `context_length - max_tokens`, and applies the same effective window to the minimum-floor/85% degeneracy guard. It propagates the resolved output cap during initialization, model switching, and fallback activation, while preserving an existing reservation when `update_model` is called without a max-token argument. Defensive coercion prevents malformed values from breaking threshold arithmetic, and pathological reservations at or above the context window safely fall back to prior full-window behavior. This addresses the reported custom-provider scenario because normal agent initialization forwards the transport-resolved `agent.max_tokens`, including the custom provider's default. All authoritative regression tests passed, including compressor tests and relevant switch/fallback/compaction-loop suites. The implementation is somewhat broader than the reference through provider-profile fallback resolution and extra lifecycle call-site changes, but these are aligned with the contract and did not introduce observed regressions.
concerns: No dedicated regression tests were added to the patch for the exact 131072/65536 reservation scenario, provider-default resolution, or malformed/pathological max-token values; validation relies on existing tests and related lifecycle suites.

`_resolve_max_tokens` dynamically imports provider profiles and catches all exceptions. This is resilient but adds coupling and can silently revert to no reservation if provider-profile resolution changes or fails.

The model-switch and fallback call-site edits are slightly broader than necessary because `update_model` can preserve the existing reservation when omitted; however, forwarding `agent.max_tokens` better mirrors the current transport state and the related regression tests pass.
Validation was focused rather than repository-wide; 133 relevant tests and diff checks passed, but no full test-suite result was provided.

judge.rationale: The patch satisfies the core postcondition: the compaction threshold is calculated from the effective input window after subtracting the resolved positive output-token reservation, and the production initialization path forwards the agent's max_tokens value. It also applies the effective window consistently to the minimum-floor/85% guard and recalculates the threshold on model updates. The custom-provider default scenario and model-switch behavior received direct integration checks, while the visible compressor suite and related context-switch/compression suites all passed. The main weaknesses are that provider-profile resolution is duplicated inside ContextCompressor rather than relying solely on the transport's already-resolved value, broad exception swallowing can hide provider-profile defects, and no permanent regression tests were added to the repository despite the behavior change.
concerns: ContextCompressor now independently imports and queries provider profiles, duplicating output-cap resolution logic that may drift from the transport's actual precedence or provider-specific behavior.

The broad `except Exception: pass` in `_resolve_max_tokens` silently converts profile lookup/programming failures into an unreserved full-window budget, potentially recreating the unsafe behavior without diagnostics.

The `_max_tokens_explicit` distinction is inferred from the value passed to the compressor. Because `init_agent` passes `agent.max_tokens`, a provider-derived default may be treated as user-explicit and retained across switches unless the switch supplies a new cap; this is not necessarily identical to transport resolution in every switching path.

No regression tests were committed. Manual checks covered the reported custom-provider reservation and switching behavior, and all relevant existing tests passed, but future protection is weaker than it would be with focused repository tests.
